name: Service Bus and RabbitMQ
tagline: An AMQP broker that answers as Azure Service Bus or RabbitMQ and shows every message with its deliveries, locks and consumers.

capabilities.title: Every message, every delivery
capabilities.text: Published, delivered, abandoned, completed or dead-lettered: each message keeps its history and properties.

capabilities.title: Queues, topics, subscriptions
capabilities.text: Namespaces with queues and topics; Service Bus subscriptions or RabbitMQ bindings fan out what is published.

capabilities.title: Consumers and their locks
capabilities.text: Who is receiving, receive mode, prefetch, the locks held now and what each consumer completed today.

capabilities.title: Rules for deliveries
capabilities.text: When op, entity and subject match: lose the lock, duplicate, hold, drop or dead-letter, the first N or a share.

capabilities.title: Dead-letter and resubmit
capabilities.text: See why a message was dead-lettered, move one there by hand, or put them all back on their queue.

capabilities.title: Publish as a partner
capabilities.text: publish puts a message on a queue or topic with subject, properties, session or schedule; it is marked as yours.

capabilities.title: RabbitMQ management API
capabilities.text: MassTransit and provisioning scripts create vhosts, queues, exchanges and bindings on :15672 before they connect. Open connections are listed and can be closed; every user, password and permission change lands on the Timeline with who made it.

capabilities.title: Namespace-wide trouble
capabilities.text: Refuse connections, time out, reject the key, answer ServerBusy, cap the throughput or turn off auto-create.

callouts.title: Both brokers
callouts.text: Service Bus and RabbitMQ namespaces side by side, with queues, topics and subscriptions.

callouts.title: Counts by state
callouts.text: Active, scheduled, locked and dead-letter for the entity.

callouts.title: Next delivery
callouts.text: Lose the lock, duplicate, hold, drop or dead-letter the next delivery, once.

callouts.title: Locked
callouts.text: Which consumer holds the lock and how long it has left.

callouts.title: Delivery history
callouts.text: Published, delivered, abandoned with the handler's error, then completed on attempt 2.

excerpts.title: Consumers, and how to knock them over

callouts.title: Receiving now
callouts.text: Each connection with prefetch and receive mode; names come from the AMQP client id.

callouts.title: Disconnected
callouts.text: Consumers that left in the last day, and why.

callouts.title: Disconnect it
callouts.text: A forced detach (or CONNECTION_FORCED on RabbitMQ) tests the app's reconnect logic.

callouts.title: Expire its locks
callouts.text: Its next complete fails with MessageLockLost and the messages come again.

callouts.title: Locks held
callouts.text: The messages this consumer has locked and the time left on each.

excerpts.title: A rule, tried on real traffic before you save

callouts.title: When
callouts.text: Operation, namespace, entity and subject; more conditions on properties, session, size or sender.

callouts.title: Instead
callouts.text: What happens to the matching delivery: here the lock is lost and the message comes again.

callouts.title: How often
callouts.text: The first N, every time, or a random share of deliveries.

callouts.title: Try it
callouts.text: How many of the last 50 deliveries would match, and which ones.

callouts.title: What the app will see
callouts.text: Lock lost after 30 s and redelivered, then back to normal.

provoke.name: Lost lock
provoke.what: The next delivery loses its lock and comes again

provoke.name: Duplicate delivery
provoke.what: The same message is delivered twice

provoke.name: Held, dropped or out of order
provoke.what: Delivery waits 30 s, never comes, or overtakes another

provoke.name: Dead-lettered on arrival
provoke.what: The message goes straight to the dead-letter queue

provoke.name: MessageLockLost on complete
provoke.what: Locks a consumer holds expire now

provoke.name: Namespace down
provoke.what: Connections refused, time out, 401 or ServerBusy

provoke.name: Throttled
provoke.what: ServerBusy over N messages a second, or every send

provoke.name: Rotated key
provoke.what: Senders still on the old key get 401

provoke.name: Missing entity
provoke.what: Queues the app did not declare answer 404

provoke.name: Rule on deliveries
provoke.what: Any of the above for matching messages, first N or a share

advantages.title: No cloud namespace
advantages.text: No Azure subscription, no RabbitMQ container: one process speaks both, with the same connection strings.

advantages.title: See inside the broker
advantages.text: Every delivery, lock and consumer is visible, which a real broker only gives through metrics.

advantages.title: Hard cases on cue
advantages.text: Lost locks, duplicates and forced detaches happen on the next delivery instead of once a month in production.

advantages.title: Rules tried first
advantages.text: A rule shows which recent deliveries it would hit before you save it, and never touches other environments.

agent.prompt: Make sure the order worker handles a lost lock without processing the order twice.
